questions.question: On selling of 18 pens at Rs.360, there is a loss equal to the cost of 3 pens. What is the cost price of a pen?
questions.solution:
Given:

Loss on selling 18 pens = CP of 3 pens.

Concept used:

Loss = CP - SP

Calculation:

(C.P. of 18 pens) - (S.P. of 18 pens) = (C.P. of 3 pens)

⇒ CP of 15 pens = SP of 18 pens

⇒ CP (1 pen)/SP (1 pen) = 18/15 = 6/5

According to the question,

SP (1 pen) = 360/18 = 20

∴ CP of 1 pen = 6/5 × 20 = 24

**∴ Option 3 is the correct answer.**

questions.question: The cost of 3 cups and 5 plates is ₹1,080 and the cost of 2 cups and 4 plates is ₹840. Find the ratio of the cost of a cup to the cost of a plate.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

2 Cups + 4 Plates = 840 → 1 Cup + 2 Plates = 420.

Multiply by 3 ⇒ 3 Cups + 6 Plates = 1260.

Difference with (3 Cups + 5 Plates = 1080) ⇒ 1 Plate = 1260 − 1080 = 180.

Cost of 1 Cup = 420 − (2 × 180) = 420 − 360 = 60.

Ratio of Cup to Plate = 60 : 180 = 1 : 3.

**∴ The correct answer is 1 ∶ 3.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost of 3 cups and 5 plates = ₹1,080

Cost of 2 cups and 4 plates = ₹840

**Formula Used:**

Simultaneous Linear Equations: a₁x + b₁y = c₁ and a₂x + b₂y = c₂

 
 3 Cups + 5 Plates
 
• 
 ₹1080
 
 2 Cups + 4 Plates
 
• 
 ₹840
 Ratio Required = Cost of Cup : Cost of Plate

Let the cost of one cup be C and the cost of one plate be P.

⇒ 3C + 5P = 1080 ... (i)

⇒ 2C + 4P = 840 ... (ii)

⇒ From (ii), C + 2P = 420 ⇒ C = 420 − 2P

⇒ Substitute C in (i): 3 × (420 − 2P) + 5P = 1080

⇒ 1260 − 6P + 5P = 1080

⇒ 1260 − P = 1080

⇒ P = 1260 − 1080 = 180

⇒ C = 420 − 2 × 180 = 420 − 360 = 60

⇒ Ratio C : P = 60 : 180

⇒ C : P = 1 : 3

**∴ The correct answer is 1 ∶ 3.**

**__Additional Information__**

Linear Equations in Two Variables

An equation of the form ax + by + c = 0 where a, b, and c are real numbers and a, b ≠ 0.

Ratio and Proportion

A ratio is a comparison of two quantities by division, denoted as a : b or a/b. It has no units if both quantities have the same unit.

Elimination Method

A method of solving simultaneous equations by making the coefficients of one variable equal to eliminate it by addition or subtraction.

questions.question: Ravi buys salt at ₹16 per kg and sells it at ₹18 per kg. He also uses the weight of 900 gm instead of 1000 gm. What is Ravi's actual profit percentage?

**Calculations:**

When he sells 1 kg = 1000gm

Actual quantity he gave = 900gm.

SP = 1000(18) = 18000

Effective CP = 900(16) = 14400

Hence, profit % = ((SP - CP)/CP) × 100

= ((18000 - 14400)/14400)100 

= (3600/14400)100 = 25%

**Hence, The Required value is 25%.**

questions.question: A person purchased a table and a sofa for ₹28,000. He sold the sofa at a profit of 10% and the table at a profit 15.25%. If his total profit was 13%, then the difference between the cost price of the sofa and the table (in ₹) is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the Alligation Method directly on profit percentages to find the ratio of their Cost Prices (CP):

Ratio of CP of Sofa to Table = (Table Profit % − Overall Profit %) : (Overall Profit % − Sofa Profit %)

⇒ Ratio = (15.25 − 13) : (13 − 10) = 2.25 : 3 = 225 : 300 = 3 : 4

Total CP parts = 3 + 4 = 7 parts ⇒ 7 parts = ₹28,000

⇒ 1 part = ₹4,000

Difference in CP = 4 parts − 3 parts = 1 part = ₹4,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹4000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Total Cost Price (CP) of Sofa and Table = ₹28,000

⇒ Profit percentage on selling the Sofa = 10%

⇒ Profit percentage on selling the Table = 15.25%

⇒ Overall profit percentage on both = 13%

**Formula Used:**

We apply the Rule of Alligation to find the ratio of the Cost Prices of the two articles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4c4e22d74f4ad4aef6134dfe43f8bed451703a553b1c2325902048cf0ae7e099.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the CP of the Sofa be 3x and the CP of the Table be 4x.

⇒ Total CP = 3x + 4x = 7x

⇒ 7x = 28000

⇒ x = 28000 ÷ 7 = 4000

⇒ Required difference in CP = CP of Table − CP of Sofa

⇒ Difference = 4x − 3x = x

⇒ Difference = ₹4000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹4000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Rule of Alligation in Profit & Loss

When two items are mixed or sold together at different profit/loss percentages, applying the alligation method yields the ratio of their Base Values, which is the Cost Price (CP) for profit and loss scenarios.

Weighted Average Formula

The overall profit percentage is the weighted average of the individual profit percentages. Formula: Overall % = (CP₁ × P₁ + CP₂ × P₂) ÷ (CP₁ + CP₂).

Handling Loss in Alligation

If an item is sold at a loss, its percentage must be written with a negative sign (e.g., −10%) in the alligation cross. The arithmetic difference must be carefully calculated considering the negative sign.

questions.question: An article is sold at a certain price. If it is sold at 70% of this price, then there is a loss of 10%. What is the percentage profit, when it is sold at the original selling price?
questions.solution:
Given:

If the article is sold at 70% of this price, then there is a loss of 10%.

Concept used:

Selling Price = Cost Price × (1 - Loss%)

Selling Price = Cost Price - Cost Price × Loss%

Profit% = {(Selling Price - Cost Price) over Cost Price} times 100\%

Calculation:

Let the article be originally sold for 100p.

If it is sold at 70% of this price, the selling price would be

⇒ 100p × 70% = 70p

Let the cost price of the article be Q.

According to the concept,

Q - Q × 10% = 70p

⇒ Q - 0.1Q = 70p

⇒ 0.9Q = 70p

⇒ Q = 70p/0.9

⇒ Q = 700p/9

Now, the profit% when it's sold at the original selling price = {{100p - {700p over 9}} over {700p over 9}} times 100\%

⇒ ​(200)/(7)%

**∴ ​(200)/(7)% is the percentage profit when it is sold at the original selling price.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__**Let the article be originally sold for Rs. 900.

If it is sold at 70% of this price, the selling price would be

⇒ 900 × 70% = Rs. 630

So, the cost price of the article = 630 ÷ 0.9 = Rs. 700

Now, the profit% when it's sold at the original selling price = {{900 - 700} over 700} times 100\%

⇒ ​(200)/(7)%

∴ ​(200)/(7)% is the percentage profit when it is sold at the original selling price.

questions.question: A retailer marks up the price of his goods by 30%. He sells 50% of his goods at a discount of 8% and the remaining at a discount of 6%. Find his profit percentage.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Marked price = 130% of cost price

Discount% = 8% & 6% for 50% goods

**Formula used:**

Marked price = [Marked% / 100] x CP

Selling price = [Discount% / 100] x MP

Profit % = (Profit / Cost Price) x 100

Profit = SP - CP

**Solution:**

Let, cost price = CP 

So, marked price = 130/100 x CP = 1.3CP

The selling price of 50% goods at an 8% discount = [{{{(100-8) over 100} times 1.3CP} over 2}]

= 0.46 x 1.3CP = 0.598CP

The selling price of 50% goods at a 6% discount = [{{{(100-6) over 100} times 1.3CP} over 2}]

= 0.47 x 1.3CP = 0.611CP

Total selling price = (0.598+0.611)CP = 1.209CP

Profit = SP - CP = 1.209CP - CP = 0.209CP

**Profit% = [0.209CP / CP] x 100 = 20.9%**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__**

**Concept Used:**

Weighted average for profit calculations.

**Calculation:**

Assume cost price of goods = 100 units

Markup = 30% of cost price

⇒ Marked price = 130 units

Selling price of first half of goods = 92% of marked price (due to 8% discount)

⇒ Effective selling price for this half = 0.92 × 130 = 119.6 units

Selling price of second half of goods = 94% of marked price (due to 6% discount)

⇒ Effective selling price for this half = 0.94 × 130 = 122 units

The average selling price (considering equal quantity sold at both discounts)

⇒ (119.6 + 122) / 2 = 120.8 units

Profit percentage = ((Selling price - Cost price) / Cost price) × 100

⇒ Profit percentage = ((120.8 - 100) / 100) × 100 = 20.9%

**Therefore, the retailer makes a profit of 20.9%.**
